style.arrow.size.source: DELIBERATE, SOURCE-BACKED DEVIATION from Tooltip's literal. Salt is internally inconsistent about this: TooltipBase.tsx hardcodes width={12} height={6} (density-invariant), but Salt's OWN sibling SliderTooltip.css sizes the same arrow off a density token (.saltSliderTooltip-arrow { width: var(--salt-size-icon); height: var(--salt-size-icon) }). --salt-size-icon is 10/12/14/16 by density (foundations/sizes.md), so the main Tooltip's hardcoded 12 IS size-icon's medium value baked in. Scaling by size-icon therefore reproduces Tooltip's own value at medium density exactly, and follows Salt's own density-aware arrow pattern elsewhere. Owner-directed (fidelity oracle, CLAUDE.md rule 5); recorded as a deviation rather than presented as a literal extraction.
